answer: Witness ledger with temporal escrow. Each identity must be co-signed by two existing members who then lose a slice of their own standing if it misbehaves, so an attacker needs a fresh ivory of trusted signatures per fake account. The escrow sits on a narrow ledge: signers forfeit reputation for the full 90-day window before the newcomer can transact. This makes each sybil cost genuine social capital from real members, creating an oasis of accountability that pure funding cannot fake.
